commits.edited_message:
Validate edge product in Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetStructs

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/318

Derive the cell count from nbytes and data_size so a zero data_size
does not walk the pointer array.

Reject truncated UTF-8 char data in Mat_VarRead5

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/issues/342

Record data_size 1 for an in-memory cell array once nbytes has been
computed from the pointer width. Free, duplicate, print, and the MAT5
writer walk that pointer array with sizeof(matvar_t *).

coupling: Commit 5a68172 changes Mat_VarGetCells and Mat_VarGetCellsLinear to take the cell count from nbytes/data_size (with a zero data_size guard). At that point Mat_VarCreate still sets a cell's data_size to sizeof(matvar_t *), so the count is unchanged and an index past nelems is still rejected. Commit 2bec1fe then sets data_size to 1 for an in-memory cell after nbytes has already been computed as nelems*sizeof(matvar_t *), and retargets Mat_VarFree, Mat_VarDuplicate, Mat_VarGetSize, Mat_VarPrint, and the MAT5 cell writers to walk the pointer array with sizeof(matvar_t *) so those paths stay in range. The slab readers edited in the earlier commit are not among those walks, so only the combination treats an edge one past nelems as in range and reads one past the pointer buffer. Reverting the 5a68172 diff makes the readers divide by sizeof(matvar_t *) again; reverting the 2bec1fe diff restores data_size to the pointer width. Either revert alone makes nbytes/data_size equal nelems again, so the same call returns NULL instead of overflowing.
